privacy.title: Privacy policy
privacy.description: What catena collects, what we don't do with it, where data lives, your access / correction / deletion rights under Loi 25 + PIPEDA.
privacy.intro: Catena does not share, sell, rent, or train AI on your data. The whole point of the suite is that you own it.
privacy.collect_body: Contact details and support requests. Payment goes through Polar, the merchant of record, which holds the payment details: card numbers never touch our servers. For clients who subscribe to the central audit log copy, the suite's administrative audit entries (each admin action, who took it, from which address), kept 90 days. The suite's data, its backups, the key that opens them and the credentials of its provider accounts stay on the client's own server and accounts, and never reach our systems.
privacy.dont_body: We do not sell, rent, or share your data. We do not train AI models on it. We do not analyze it for advertising. We do not use third-party trackers on the marketing site.
privacy.where_body: Your suite data lives on the server you own, the S3 bucket you own, and the third-party accounts you yourself selected (Cloudflare, Tailscale, your VPS provider, your SMTP provider, etc.).
privacy.subprocessors_body: Polar (payment and sales tax, as merchant of record). Cloudflare (Tunnel + edge for catena.run). The providers chosen for a suite are the client's own, contracted directly by the client.
privacy.rights_body: Law 25 and PIPEDA grant you the right to access, correct, and delete personal information we hold. Contact privacy@catena.run (or hello@catena.run interim) and we will respond within 30 days.
privacy.cookies_body: No third-party trackers, no advertising cookies, no cookies on the marketing site. Aggregate visit analytics on the marketing site via a self-hosted Plausible instance -- no cookies, no fingerprinting, no personal data; Law 25 / GDPR compliant with no consent banner required.
privacy.contact_body: Email hello@catena.run. We answer privacy questions within one business day.

terms.title: Terms of service
terms.description: Catena's terms of service. Service scope, pricing and billing, data ownership, acceptable use, termination, governing law (Quebec, Canada).
terms.intro: These terms cover the relationship between Catena (the service provider) and you (the client). They are deliberately concise -- the engagement letter you sign at signup is the canonical contract; this page summarizes its main commitments.
terms.review_notice: This page is a draft pending legal review. Talk to us directly for the binding terms in your engagement letter.
terms.scope_body: The subscription, Catena Pro or Catena Business -- one flat price per server, unlimited apps -- defines what is included, with hands-on support billed hourly as used. See the pricing section for the public model. Changes to scope are agreed in writing.
terms.billing_body: The managed subscription is one flat retainer per server, billed monthly, with no minimum term. Hands-on support is billed at the published rate in 15-minute increments, as used. Payment and sales tax via Polar, the merchant of record.
terms.ownership_body: All client data, infrastructure, and credentials belong to the client and stay on the client's own server and accounts. Our role is service provider only. Export and migration need nothing from us.
terms.liability_body: Liability is capped at amounts proportionate to the most recent monthly retainer; the binding limits are set out in your engagement letter.
terms.sla_body: Target uptime, response times, and recovery objectives for restore drills are set out in your engagement letter and reviewed at the quarterly check-in.
terms.aup_body: No illegal content, no unsolicited bulk email (spam), no malware distribution, no resale of the suite as-a-service to third parties without prior agreement. Standard internet-services posture.
terms.termination_body: Either party may terminate per the engagement letter. The suite, its data and its backups stay with the client: nothing needs handing over.
terms.perservice_body: Each upstream app in the suite carries its own license and acceptable-use policy (Nextcloud GPL, Rocket.Chat MIT, Euro Office AGPL, etc.). Each upstream's official terms are linked from that app's documentation.
terms.law_body: Quebec, Canada. Disputes go to the courts of the judicial district of Montreal.

status.title: Service status
status.description: Real-time status of Catena services (catena.run, the docs, the billing API). Uptime probed 24/7 by Gatus, on a host separate from the application server. If the main site goes down, this page stays up.
status.intro: Public uptime of Catena services. Refreshed minute-by-minute by Gatus.
status.what_body_1: This page shows real-time status of the services Catena operates for ourselves -- the marketing site (catena.run), the docs (docs.catena.run), and the billing API.
status.what_body_2: Gatus probes run on a host separate from the one serving the apps, so this page stays consultable even if a primary service goes down. Any outage hitting Catena infrastructure is publicly visible; we can't hide it.
status.what_body_3: For clients on a retainer, SLA thresholds depend on your tier (Small: best-effort; Medium / Large: 99.5%).
status.dashboard_body: Embed coming once Gatus is publicly exposed at https://status.catena.run. In the meantime, email hello@catena.run or book a call if you suspect an outage.
status.placeholder: Status: in build. The public Gatus dashboard will be embedded here in the next iteration. The internal Gatus instance is already running and powering operator alerts.
